newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end down on correction.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end down on correction.

text.p: China's A and B shares indices ended down in slow trade on Friday on a technical correction after gains over the past few days, with investors cautious over unpromising company results for 1996, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index fell 0.337 point or 0.46 percent to 72.936 on volume of 14.8 million shares worth $6.3 million.

Brokers said that domestic investors were not satisfied with the dividend plan of Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development despite a surge in its net profit, and this led to falls in both Pudong shares and the index.

Shanghai Jinqiao was the biggest loser in both the A and B share markets. Its B share fell $0.02 or 3.44 percent to $0.56 on volume of 432,400 shares and its A share were down 1.13 yuan or 6.5 percent to 16.23 yuan on volume of 3.6 million shares.

Toy maker Shanghai Haixin traded the most on active buying spurred by the group's 1996 results and dividend plan, brokers said. It rose $0.008 or 1.25 percent to $0.644 on volume of 1.8 million shares.

Haixin's 1996 net profit was 75.139 million yuan ($9.07 million), up 53.81 percent from 48.851 million yuan in 1995, according to international accounting standards, due to good management which guaranteed sales and quality, its annual report said on Friday.
Shenzhen's B share market was closed in line with the Hong Kong stock exchange Easter holiday. Trading will resume next Tuesday, exchange officials said.

Despite the suspension of B share trading, the exchange system indicated that some trades in B shares were done in the first 10 minutes in the morning session, pushing the index up 0.42 points to 162.56 points on apparent turnover of HK$1.1 million.
A lack of coordination among different departments at the exchange led to the confusion, officials said.
Shanghai's A index slipped 12.295 points or 0.97 percent to 1,259.317 points on volume of 714.7 million shares worth 8.3 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue chip index fell 34.835 points or 1.02 percent to 3,384.134 points.
Shenzhen's A share index shook off 3.58 points or 0.80 percent to 446.74 points.
